d: Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. We specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today's needs and transition to more sustainable solutions.

The Contract Manager is responsible for leading the development, tendering, award, administration, and close-out of all project-related contracts required to support successful project delivery. The role provides commercial and contractual leadership across the full contract lifecycle, ensuring that contracting strategies, commercial governance, contract administration, change management, claims management, and contractor performance management are executed effectively and in accordance with project and client requirements.

The role is responsible for the management of contracts placed by the project on either Worley paper or Customer paper, including engineering, procurement, construction, fabrication, specialist services, and other third-party agreements. The role does not include ownership or administration of the prime contract between Worley and the Customer.
q: Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Law, Business, Commerce, or a related discipline.
Professional qualification in Commercial Management, Contract Management, Quantity Surveying, Procurement, or Law is preferred.
Membership of a recognised professional institution is desirable.
Minimum 15 years of experience in contract management, commercial management, procurement, or project services within the Oil & Gas, Energy, Petrochemical, Infrastructure, or Industrial sectors.
Demonstrable experience managing high-value engineering, construction, fabrication, and service contracts on major capital projects.
Experience supporting the full contract lifecycle from strategy development through contract close-out.
Proven experience leading commercial negotiations, tender evaluations, and contractor selection processes.
Strong experience managing contract changes, variations, claims, and dispute resolution activities.
Experience working within EPC, EPCM, PMC, or Owner's Team project delivery environments.
Experience managing multiple contractors and complex stakeholder interfaces on large-scale projects.
Experience working on international projects and within multicultural delivery teams.
Previous Middle East experience is preferred.
Iraq project experience or experience operating within challenging international environments is highly desirable.
Strong understanding of contract law and commercial management principles.
Extensive knowledge of international forms of contract, including EPC, EPCM, reimbursable, lump-sum, unit-rate, and target-cost contracting models.
Strong understanding of project risk management and commercial governance practices.
Ability to evaluate contractual risk and develop mitigation strategies.
Excellent negotiation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced project environment.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
High level of commercial acumen and business judgement.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and contract management systems.
Safe execution of all contracting and commercial activities.
Timely award and administration of project contracts.
Effective management of contractual risk and commercial exposure.
Successful resolution of contract changes and claims.
Compliance with project governance and contractual requirements.
Achievement of project cost, schedule, and performance objectives.
Strong contractor and stakeholder relationships that support successful project delivery.

r: Demonstrate visible HSSE leadership and promote a culture of safety, integrity, compliance, and ethical business conduct.
Lead the development and execution of the project's contracting and commercial strategy.
Establish and maintain contract management processes, procedures, governance, and commercial controls.
Provide contractual and commercial leadership to the project management team throughout all project phases.
Ensure all contracting activities support project objectives relating to cost, schedule, quality, risk, and delivery.
Lead tendering, evaluation, negotiation, award, and administration of major contracts and service agreements.
Protect the project's commercial interests through effective management of contractual obligations, risks, claims, and changes.
Support project leadership in commercial decision-making and contractor engagement.
Ensure compliance with company policies, client requirements, local regulations, and applicable governance frameworks.
Develop and maintain strong working relationships with contractors, suppliers, client representatives, project teams, and key stakeholders.
Develop and implement project contracting plans and execution strategies.
Identify optimum contract models and compensation mechanisms to support project delivery objectives.
Lead sourcing and contracting activities for engineering, construction, fabrication, specialist services, equipment, and other project requirements.
Prepare, review, and issue Invitation to Tender (ITT) documentation and associated commercial requirements.
Coordinate tender evaluations and ensure robust commercial assessment of bidders.
Lead commercial clarifications, negotiations, and contract award recommendations.
Support project leadership in contractor selection and commercial decision-making.
Administer contracts throughout the full contract lifecycle from award through completion and close-out.
Ensure contractual obligations and deliverables are clearly defined, monitored, and effectively managed.
Maintain contract registers, obligations registers, commercial correspondence logs, and supporting documentation.
Provide interpretation and guidance on contractual terms and conditions to project teams and stakeholders.
Ensure contractual compliance by both the project and contractors.
Manage contractual and commercial risks through identification, assessment, mitigation, and ongoing monitoring.
Lead management of contract changes, variations, compensation events, amendments, and supplemental agreements.
Review and assess contractor commercial submissions, invoices, payment applications, and entitlement claims.
Support cost control and project controls teams in the management of commercial commitments and forecasting.
Provide commercial input into budget reviews, project forecasts, and business reporting requirements.
Lead the preparation, assessment, defence, negotiation, and resolution of contractual claims.
Develop strategies to minimise commercial exposure and avoid disputes where possible.
Support dispute resolution processes and provide commercial recommendations to project leadership.
Maintain appropriate records to support contractual positions and commercial decisions.
Monitor contractor compliance with contractual obligations and project requirements.
Participate in contractor performance reviews and commercial audits.
Promote continuous improvement in contracting processes and commercial governance.
Prepare contractual and commercial reports for project and business leadership.
Support contract close-out activities, final account negotiations, and lessons learned reviews.

r: Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Manama, Bahrain, and in collaboration with relevant units at the Regional Office, Headquarters and the Administrative Centres, the successful candidate will be responsible and accountable for managing the resources management functions in IOM Bahrain Country Office.
Provide overall support to the Resources Management Unit (RMU) in financial, procurement, human resources and other administrative activities;

Assist with the monitoring of and process and reconcile financial transactions and payments to staff and suppliers in a timely manner, maintain financial records using the IOM Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) System in line with IOM financial regulations;
Assist in the monitoring of budget versus actual financials for the operational activities of the Regional Office or Country Office;
Review validity checks on monthly payroll projectization results of the Regional Office or Country Office;
Review the imprest accounts and guarantee the safe custody of all available cash;
Contribute to the preparation of the Regional Office or Country Office monthly accounts closure in compliance with the accounts closure checklist;
Contribute to the preparation of budgets and accounting, financial, statistical and donor reports complying with relevant donor requirements;
Maintain a filing system and ensure that all RMU documents and paid vouchers are properly filed and updated in the order in which they are entered in PRISM;

Validate that all Travel Authorizations are duly completed before staff are authorized to travel and validate that all TAs and expense claims are duly completed and all supporting documents are attached prior to dispatch for computation and reimbursement.
Provide general guidance and oversight on accounting, financial policies and procedures to the Regional Office or Country Office Units as required;
Assist with the management of the office asset inventory in line with IOM Assets inventory policy and maintain an updated asset inventory report;

Oversee procurement activities including obtaining quotations, preparing evaluations and recommendations, issuing Purchase Requisitions (PR) Purchase Orders (PO) or Service Agreements (SA) and delivery of goods/services in accordance to IOM procurement guidelines;
Liaise with the Regional Offices, Country Offices, MAC and PAC with regard to the financial and administrative activities as required;
Perform other duties as may be assigned.
